In an affine transformation, the bottom row of the matrix is strictly locked to [O, @ , 1] . Therefore, the denominator is always exactly 1, causing uniform scaling across the entire image. In a projective transformation, the denominator fluctuates depending on the x and y values of the specific point being processed. As points "move further away" in the virtual space, the denominator grows larger, causing the resulting x' and y' coordinates to shrink closer together.
